title: Alice's bit away from the special coordinate
statement: Let $\omega$ be a sample of the hard distribution, with special coordinate $T$, per-coordinate assignment $\text{other}$, and let $\text{xBit}(\omega, i)$ denote Alice's bit at coordinate $i$. Then for every coordinate $i \neq T$, Alice's bit at $i$ equals Alice's bit in the disjoint coordinate-pair $\text{other}(i)$ that $\omega$ assigns to $i$.
hypotheses_covered: the coordinate i is distinct from the special coordinate T
